text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Wednesday:
- Abraham Burg, president of the Jewish Agency, again strongly criticised Switzerland and Swiss banks, saying that 'neutral Switzerland was the bank of the Nazis'.
- The U.S. State Department commented too quickly on Swiss Ambassador Carlo Jagmetti's resignation, making the current situation between Berne and Washington more tense.
- The Swiss Cheese Union wants to deregulate the cheese market earlier than planned and will file for deregulation on August 1.
- Pharmaceuticals group Novartis posted a moderate sales increase of eight percent to 27.6 billion Swiss francs for 1996.
- "Swissbau 97", the annual trade show for Switzerland's building industry featuring more than 1,000 firms, opened on Tuesday in Basle.
- Swiss President Flavio Cotti pleaded for Switzerland to avoid further isolation and to move faster towards joining the European Union and other multilateral organisations.
- Greenpeace activists protested against Nestle's and Switzerland's importation of genetically altered soy beans by setting up a feast at the Nestle headquarters parking lot in Vevey.
- Schenker Maschinen AG and Schenker Technik AG in Gretzenbach, canton Solothurn, filed for bankruptcy.
- Heberlein Textildruck AG is cutting 95 of its 470 jobs due to the shrinking market demand.
- Chocolate factory Lindt & Sprungli's consolidated sales rose by 5.8 percent to 973 million Swiss francs in 1996.
- Israeli President Ezer Weizman said he will not participate in the 100th anniversary celebration of the Basle Zionist Congress, saying his absence has nothing to do with recent bank controversies.
